keywords.assert: assert EXPR; - trap with 'assertion failed' when EXPR is 0
keywords.const: const NAME = EXPR; - compile-time constant (costs no register)
keywords.continue: continue; - next iteration (runs the for step)
keywords.do: do { ... } while (COND); / do { ... } until (COND); - body runs at least once
keywords.exit: exit [EXPR]; - end the whole program from anywhere
keywords.fn: fn NAME(params) { ... } - define a function (0..16 integer parameters, returns an integer)
keywords.for: for (INIT; COND; STEP) STMT - each part optional; a let in INIT is loop-scoped
keywords.if: if (COND) STMT [elsif (COND) STMT]... [else STMT]; also a statement modifier: STMT if COND;
keywords.let: let NAME = EXPR; - declare a block-scoped variable
keywords.my: my NAME = EXPR; - synonym for let
keywords.print: print EXPR, ...; - output each value on its own line
keywords.return: return [EXPR]; - return from a function; at top level, end the program with EXPR as result
keywords.unless: unless (COND) STMT [else STMT] - if (!COND); also a modifier: STMT unless COND;
keywords.use: use LIB, ...; - import a library (its public fn and const become visible, also as LIB::name)

checked.doc:
checked: overflow detection, saturating and trapping arithmetic.

     use checked;
     let a = 3037000500;
     print mul_ok(a, a);                // 0: a * a overflows
     print add_sat(INT_MAX, 1);         // INT_MAX
     print add_checked(a, 1);           // traps if the sum overflows

*_ok return 1 when the operation is exact, *_sat clamp to the int64
range, *_checked assert exactness.

date.doc:
date: proleptic Gregorian calendar arithmetic.

     use date;
     let d = days_from_civil(2024, 2, 29);        // days since 1970-01-01
     print day_of_week(2024, 2, 29), civil(d + 1), easter(2025);

Dates are passed as (year, month, day) with months 1..12, or packed as
the integer YYYYMMDD (20240301) by civil(), pack() and add_days().
Weekdays are 0 = Sunday .. 6 = Saturday.

fixed.doc:
fixed: Q16.16 fixed-point arithmetic in a 64-bit integer.

     use fixed;
     let r = from_ratio(3, 2);                  // 1.5
     print to_milli(mul(r, r)), to_milli(sqrt(from_int(2)));   // 2250 1414

A value v represents v / 65536. Products are exact up to about 2**47 in
magnitude; mul/div truncate toward zero; floor/ceil/round return fixed
values.

geom: integer 2-D geometry on separate x, y coordinates.

     use geom;
     print manhattan(0, 0, 3, 4), dist(0, 0, 3, 4), orient(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1);  // 7 5 1

Exact integer predicates (orientation, intersection) are robust; dist()
is the floor of the Euclidean distance.

math: integer arithmetic.

     use math;
     print gcd(84, 36), isqrt(1000), clamp(42, 0, 10);   // 12 31 10

All arithmetic is signed 64-bit and wraps on overflow, so abs(INT_MIN)
is INT_MIN. Functions that need a precondition (isqrt of a negative
number, ilog2 of zero) assert it.

units.doc:
units: unit conversions in scaled integers.

     use units;
     print c_to_f(37000), miles_to_m(26), kib(64), deg_to_mrad(180);   // 98600 41842 65536 3141

Temperatures are in thousandths of a degree (37000 = 37.000 C), lengths
in metres or millimetres, masses in grams, angles in degrees or
milliradians, data sizes in bytes. Conversions truncate toward zero.
